sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary + Investment Thesis**

TCS reported a 6.0% growth in revenue from operations to ₹255,324 crore in FY 2025, driven by a strong and resilient order book despite increased macroeconomic uncertainty. The company's EBIT margins stood at 24.3% in FY 2025, with a 30-basis point decline compared to the previous year, influenced by headwinds from merit-based interventions and investments in infrastructure and capability building. However, tailwinds such as improved utilization, productivity, and realization, along with favorable currency movements, contributed positively to the margins. The constant currency revenue growth for the year was 4.2%, with a positive impact of 1.8% on reported revenue due to currency movements.

Our investment thesis is based on TCS' ability to navigate the challenging global economic environment, driven by its diversified revenue streams, strong segmental performance, and focus on continuous transformation. With a significant presence in key industries such as Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (37.0% of revenue), and a growing presence in emerging areas like Communication, Media, and Technology (18.0% of revenue), TCS is well-positioned to capitalize on opportunities for resilience and recovery. The company's investment strategy, focused on optimizing working capital and achieving higher yields, is expected to drive improved overall returns. With a strong order book and a proven track record of adapting to changing market dynamics, we believe TCS is an attractive investment opportunity in the current environment.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body:
TCS is an IT services, consulting, and business solutions organization that has been partnering with the world's largest businesses for 57 years. The company offers a comprehensive portfolio of services and offerings, including application development and management, digital transformation, AI, data and cloud services, engineering services, cognitive business operations, cybersecurity, and products & platforms. TCS' geographic footprint covers multiple regions, including North America, Latin America, the United Kingdom, Continental Europe, Asia Pacific, India, and Middle East Africa. The company considers industry verticals as its primary go-to-market business segments, with six key vertical clusters: Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI), Manufacturing, Consumer Business, Communication, Media and Technology (CMT), Life Sciences and Healthcare, and Others.

The segment breakdown for TCS reveals that the company generated revenue from operations of ₹2,55,324 crore for the year ended March 31, 2025, with the BFSI segment being the largest contributor at ₹94,597 crore, followed by CMT at ₹45,893 crore, and Consumer Business at ₹40,197 crore. The segment results for these verticals were ₹25,135 crore, ₹9,582 crore, and ₹11,222 crore, respectively. The company's total segment result was ₹67,407 crore, with total unallocable expenses of ₹6,038 crore. The operating income for the year was ₹61,369 crore, with a profit before tax of ₹65,331 crore and a profit for the year of ₹48,797 crore.

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body:
The financial performance of TCS for the fiscal year 2025 (FY 2025) is characterized by a 6.0% growth in revenue from operations, which stood at ₹255,324 crore. This growth is attributed to both business growth and the impact of exchange rate movements, with the latter contributing 1.8% to the reported revenue. On a constant currency basis, the revenue growth was 4.2%. The company's earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) were ₹62,165 crore, representing 24.3% of revenue from operations. The profit after tax attributable to shareholders of the company was ₹48,553 crore, resulting in a basic earnings per share of ₹134.19.

The segment-wise performance of the company indicates that the Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance segment was the largest contributor to revenue from operations, with ₹94,597 crore. The segment results for each of the business segments are as follows: Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (₹25,135 crore), Manufacturing (₹8,225 crore), Consumer Business (₹11,222 crore), Communication, Media, and Technology (₹9,582 crore), Life Sciences and Healthcare (₹7,448 crore), and Others (₹5,795 crore). The total unallocable expenses for the year were ₹6,038 crore. However, the net worth (shareholders' equity) of the company is not provided in the given excerpts, and therefore, cannot be commented upon.

sections.title: Balance Sheet Health + Cash Flow
sections.body:
The balance sheet health of TCS appears robust, with a significant amount of cash and cash equivalents of ₹8,342 crore as at March 31, 2025. The company also has a substantial amount of bank deposits of ₹7,924 crore and earmarked balances with banks of ₹1,156 crore. The total carrying value of financial assets is ₹1,11,109 crore, comprising cash and cash equivalents, bank deposits, investments, trade receivables, and other financial assets. On the liabilities side, the company has trade payables of ₹13,909 crore, lease liabilities of ₹9,392 crore, and other financial liabilities of ₹9,222 crore. The total carrying value of financial liabilities is ₹32,523 crore.

The cash flow position of the company is not explicitly disclosed in the provided excerpts. However, the company's profit for the year attributable to shareholders is ₹48,553 crore for the year ended March 31, 2025, and ₹45,908 crore for the year ended March 31, 2024, indicating a healthy profitability trend. The company's operating income is ₹61,369 crore, and it has a depreciation and amortisation expense of ₹5,242 crore. While the exact cash flow from operations is not available, the company's ability to generate significant profits and its robust balance sheet position suggest a stable cash flow situation.

sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of TCS has provided a comprehensive overview of the company's performance and outlook. According to the management, the global technology landscape demonstrated unexpected stability in 2024, despite divergent growth patterns across regions and sectors. However, the global outlook has turned negative due to governments adjusting their policy priorities, leading to unprecedented levels of uncertainty. The management expects global growth to decline to 2.8% in 2025 and 3% in 2026. In this challenging environment, TCS is well-positioned to help enterprises accelerate their adoption of AI, cloud migration, and cybersecurity management processes.

The management has identified key demand drivers that are expected to power the company's growth in FY 2026, including technology modernization and transformation, business transformation, operating model transformation, and tech-enabled sustainability. TCS has a comprehensive enterprise risk management framework in place, which encompasses risk identification, assessment, response planning, and monitoring. The company's revenue break-up by industry vertical shows that Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) segment accounted for 37.0% of the revenue, followed by Communication, Media, and Technology (CMT) at 18.0%. The management is confident that its robust risk management initiatives, coupled with its commitment to innovation and excellence, will enable the company to navigate the challenges of the IT industry and global environment, and capitalize on the opportunities that lie ahead.

sections.title: Key Risks
sections.body:
The key risks associated with TCS are multifaceted and can be categorized into several areas. Firstly, the company faces risks related to intellectual property (IP) infringement and leakage, which may lead to potential liabilities, increased litigation, and reputation impact. Additionally, litigation risks may arise from commercial disputes, alleged violation of IPR, personal data/information breach incidents/claims, and employment-related matters. These risks can result in reputation risk, legal expenses, and adverse rulings, potentially causing substantive damage. 

Other key risks include sustainability risks, such as climate change and environmental aspects, which can affect TCS' growth, profitability, and reputation due to physical risks to life and property, transition risks, and disruptions to operations. Furthermore, the company is exposed to risks associated with disruptive technologies, which can impact its business model and operations. While TCS has established various mitigation strategies, including an IP Management Framework, strong processes and controls for compliance, and investments in green initiatives, these risks still pose a significant threat to the company's long-term sustainability and success.

sections.title: Recent Developments
sections.body:
Recent Developments
TCS has demonstrated resilience in its business performance, achieving a year-over-year revenue growth of 6.0% in FY 2025, with revenue from operations reaching ₹255,324 crore. On a constant currency basis, revenue grew by 4.2%, outpacing the growth in FY 2024. The company's operating margin stood at 24.3% in FY 2025, a marginal decline of 30 basis points compared to FY 2024, primarily due to annual wage hikes, associates' promotions, and strategic investments. TCS has maintained its focus on operational excellence, cost optimization, and prudent use of working capital, resulting in robust cash conversion and increased invested funds.

The company's strong balance sheet, with zero debt, has further strengthened its return ratios. TCS has consistently delivered high shareholder returns, with its net profit (PAT) reaching ₹62,165 crore in FY 2025. The company's compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.2% over the past five financial years highlights the resilience and scalability of its business model. However, the company faces risks such as intellectual property infringement, litigation, and sustainability risks, which it mitigates through industry-leading IP management frameworks, strong processes, and governance for compliance to contractual obligations.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The bull case for TCS is supported by the company's strong and resilient order book, with revenue from operations growing 6.0% in FY 2025 to ₹255,324 crore. The growth was driven by a 16.5% increase in revenue from the Communication, Media and Technology segment, as well as a 7.1% growth in the Manufacturing segment. Additionally, the company's EBIT margins, although declining by 30 basis points to 24.3%, remain robust. The bull case assumes that TCS will continue to benefit from its diversified portfolio and strong client relationships, allowing it to navigate the challenging global economic environment and deliver above-average growth.

The bear case, on the other hand, is concerned about the impact of global economic uncertainty on TCS' revenue growth. With global growth projected to be 2.8% in 2025 and 3.0% in 2026, significantly below the 3.7% average growth rate seen from 2000 to 2019, there is a risk that enterprises will go through longer decision cycles and experience increased scrutiny on discretionary spending. This could lead to muted revenue growth for TCS, particularly in segments such as Life Sciences and Healthcare, which saw a 1.1% decline in revenue in FY 2025. The base case assumes that TCS will deliver revenue growth in line with its historical trends, with constant currency revenue growth of 4.2% in FY 2025, and that the company will continue to maintain its robust EBIT margins. However, the base case also acknowledges the risks associated with global economic uncertainty and the potential for longer decision cycles and increased scrutiny on discretionary spending.

This will require efforts in cloud migration, updating infrastructure frameworks and developing a strong data foundation. Enterprises also face a complex risk landscape with cybersecurity threats and geopolitical tensions, making them prime targets for cybercriminals due to their valuable intellectual property and customer data. Enterprises will continue to strengthen their cybersecurity management processes, leading to continued investments in security consulting services2. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine basis by the entity53? As a part of its ISO 45001:2018 compliant OHS Management System, TCS has a documented procedure to carry out assessment of work-related hazards and risks for all routine and non-routine activities carried out at any location. Hazard and risk identification is carried out by the process owners in consultation with the safety experts. The process owners are responsible to ensure adequate controls are identified and implemented to control the identified OHS risks. Mitigation plan and controls are provided to manage the identified hazards and risks based on hierarchy of controls which includes elimination, substitution, engineering controls, training and personal protective equipment. c. eval_context.content: Customer Stories A global transportation and logistics leader, serving customers in over 200 countries with services like express delivery, freight forwarding, and logistics solutions, has been facing increasing issues with porch piracy and fraud, leading to customer dissatisfaction. In 2023, the Chamber of Commerce reported approximately 44 million packages lost or stolen, amounting to US$5 billion worth of goods lost. The logistics provider sought a solution to assess risks and enhance the security of parcel delivery. It leveraged its partnership with TCS to implement an AI-powered solution that used advanced analytics and petabytes of existing data to provide actionable insights i.e. a ‘Confidence score’ that predicts shipping risks at an address-level and allows shippers to reroute high-risk packages to the logistics provider's stores or access points, preventing loss and theft. This solution enabled merchants and businesses to make smarter, safer shipping decisions even before labels are printed. Additionally, it opened up a new revenue stream for the logistics provider. The solution has a potential to save US$ 500 million annually in the industry. A leading Global Airline had an AI vision – to enable their business users to make intelligent decisions by self-servicing their data needs. However, it’s IT landscape had multiple data platforms, impacting the speed of decision making and the time-to-market, not to mention the high maintenance and licensing costs. The airline turned to its partner of three decades, TCS, to bring all functions under a unified architecture that is easy-to-manage and capable of enabling self-service analytics features. The modernization provided a business glossary for AI to understand and make meaning out of the data, enabling the business users to “talk-to-data” in natural language to derive insights at a faster pace – driving significantly faster decision making with self-service analytics. TCS delivered a highly customized No-Code data platform that replaced proprietary data tools without losing the extensive features, making information readily available and easy to use even by non-technical business users across Marketing, Customer Loyalty, Operations, Engineering, Revenue Management, and other business divisions. Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 92 Internal Financial Control Systems and their Adequacy TCS has aligned its systems of internal financial control in line with the globally accepted risk-based framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations (COSO) of the Treadway Commission. This framework of internal financial controls meets the requirement of the Companies Act, 2013. The Internal Control – Integrated Framework (the 2013 framework) is intended to increase transparency and accountability in an organization’s process of designing and implementing a system of internal control. The framework requires a company to identify and analyze risks and manage appropriate responses. The Company has successfully laid down the framework and ensured its effectiveness. TCS’ internal controls are commensurate with its size and the nature of its operations. These have been designed to provide reasonable assurance with regard to recording and providing reliable financial and operational information, complying with applicable statutes, safeguarding assets from unauthorized use, executing transactions with proper authorization and ensuring compliance with corporate policies. TCS has a well- defined delegation of power with authority limits commensurate with the responsibilities for approving engagements with all stakeholders that commit organizational resources and results in creation of assets and liabilities, income and expenditure. TCS employs an advanced Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system that connects all parts of the organization, to record data for accounting, consolidation and management information purposes. It has continued its efforts to align all its processes and controls with global best practices. TCS management assessed the effectiveness of the Company’s internal control over financial reporting [as defined in Regulation 17 of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015] as of March 31, 2025.
